body: The agent-run contract's exit grammar: the smoke's verdict and process exit follow the codes 0, 1, 2, 3 of the agent-run command line, a usage or argument fault taking its fixed code.

The agent-run harness's argument handling: any argument the smoke takes (a stand task name, a state directory) is validated against a closed allowlist before use and reaches cargo only as a test stem or a fixed build command, never as free text.

The smoke's JSON-line verdict and events: they hold harness metadata only (verb, task, outcome, counts, exit), with the raw build and session output kept unprinted; no screen content, attribute text, control value or caller-typed text reaches the verdict.

The escher-session command line the smoke drives as it stands: its roles and flags (--session and the call flags), its exit codes 0, 1, 2, 3, its stdout command result line and its stderr usage and error messages, read by the smoke to form its verdict.

The driver session socket: the smoke's session uses the one registered Unix socket as the sole listener, reachable by the owning user only, with one bounded connection at a time; the smoke adds no listener, port, IPC endpoint or credential path.

The session state directory: a caller-named, relative target/tmp path passed as a parameter, owner-only as every session's is; the socket path bound (94 bytes) refuses a too-long state directory with its session error; session cleanup deletes only its own files, non-recursively.

The session lifecycle over the socket the smoke exercises: hello, at least one call under the closed request grammar, and stop with its lifecycle reply; a session it starts is stopped by it, leaving the host idle expiry as the fallback only.

The call the smoke runs: an existing driver verb under the closed driver verb schema, its answer or refusal read by closed fields; the smoke adds no verb, refusal cause, session error, log field or span.
Environment: the driver reads only RUST_LOG; the smoke adds no environment read to the binary or harness and passes no secret.
The smoke's build of escher-session follows the locked-builds rule (the lockfile held, no dependency resolved anew).

The contract test: it runs in the CI scripts' unittest leg through a cargo shim or equivalent, live-free, pinning the smoke's arguments, exit codes and verdict shape as the agent-run verbs are pinned.

body: The new smoke entry of the agent-run contract: a verb or selection reachable by the documented invocation that builds escher-session, boots a session on a named stand task, runs at least one call, and stops it.

The smoke's JSON-line verdict and events: agent-run event lines (run.start, run.end, status and the like) are harness metadata, encoded by python3 json, carrying no element ids, app names, typed text or panic text, and no test or build output reaching them.
The agent-run exit codes 0 · 1 · 2 · 3: the smoke's exit status follows that grammar, mapping the escher-session exit statuses it reads into it.

The escher-session command line the smoke drives as it stands: start on a named app, a call such as snapshot or run, stop, and the session errors it may meet (AlreadyRunning, NoSession, Dead, Timeout) read as a failed smoke.

The session state directory: caller-named, relative under target/tmp, inside the socket path length bound, owner-only, holding the one registered session.sock; the smoke opens no new listener, port, IPC endpoint, env read or credential path.
Indirect, through the agent-run contract: agent-run holds no process and one driver runs at a time, so the smoke stops the session it booted and leaves no host behind, even when a step fails.
Indirect, through the session host it starts: a check owns its host process, reaps it on failure, and sends child streams to null or drains them while the host runs.
An empty run is never a pass: the smoke passes only on positive evidence that a booted session answered a call.
Socket session checks are unix-gated: the smoke's behaviour off unix, including the agent-run windows entry and the session host's non-unix arms, is stated rather than left to fail at random.
The named stand task the smoke boots: the seven_guis headless stand boots offline on its bundled font, with no skip.
Indirect, through the agent-run driver's build: the cargo build of escher-session the smoke runs follows the locked, host-reproducible cargo rule its legs keep.
The contract test is offline: CI scripts are unit-tested under unittest, the cargo shim is a hand-written stand-in with no mocking library, and no live session binary runs in the unittest leg.
No new CI leg: the smoke is not a leg of its own unless an existing leg must run it; the stand-repeat and test legs keep running cli_flow over the committed flows.
The smoke adds no driver verb, carrier, refusal cause, session error, log field or span: it drives the binary as it stands, and the session's stderr and log lines stay as they are.
